newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN experts return bodies of Srebrenica victims.
newsitem.headline: UN experts return bodies of Srebrenica victims.

text.p: Remains of more than 300 bodies found in mass graves after Bosnian Serbs captured the Moslem enclave of Srebrenica in 1995 were handed over to Bosnian authorities on Wednesday, officials said.
Experts from the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia (ICTY) handed over the remains, recovered from two mass graves in northeast Bosnia last year.
After performing autopsies, the ICTY kept the bodies in an improvised collective morgue in Kalesija, east of the Moslem stronghold of Tuzla, now home to some 15,000 U.S. peacekeepers.
The ICTY, based in the Hague, was set up in 1993 to investigate and try crimes committed during the 1991-95 war that followed the breakup of federal Yugoslavia.

"This is yet another sad day for my country. The Hague Tribunal representatives handed over the remains of 303 victims from mass graves in Pilice and Lazete," said Amor Masovic, head of the Bosnian office for exchange of prisoners.
The bodies, mostly reduced to bones and shreds of clothing, were wrapped in plastic bags and were to be transported to Tuzla hospital for identification.
Bosnian Serbs overran Srebrenica, then a U.N.-proclaimed safe haven, in July 1995 and expelled up to 40,000 of its Moslem women, children and elderly.

Almost two years later up to 8,000 Srebrenica men are still unaccounted for. Most are feared taken prisoner, executed and buried in mass graves by the Serbs while trying to reach government territory, in possibly the worst atrocity of the war.
Masovic said the ICTY and a Bosnian government search committee had so far collected data on 3,000 of the missing.
The bodies ICTY collected from several locations around Srebrenica showed evidence of having been shot at close range, and some had their hands tied.
"All the bodies were autopsied and the cause of the death was determined. Repeated shots were the most frequent cause. It is clear these were mass executions," Masovic told Reuters.

Bosnian Croat Drazen Erdemovic, who served with the Bosnian Serb army during the war, was sentenced last November to 10 years' imprisonment after pleading guilty to taking part in the Pilice executions.
He is the first to be tried and sentenced of over seventy Serbs, Moslems ands Croats indicted by the tribunal.
